papers.title: The Iterative Equivariant Filter
papers.abstract: This paper presents the iterative equivariant filter (IterEqF). The iterative extended Kalman filter (IterEKF) replaces the standard EKF correction step with an iterative correction step that is the Gauss-Newton solution to a nonlinear weighted least squares problem. The standard equivariant filter (EqF) exploits and respects the underlying symmetry of state estimation problems posed on homogeneous spaces and Lie groups. The motivation behind the IterEqF is to combine the features of both the IterEKF and the EqF, thus leading to a high-performance state estimation solution that is well suited to navigation problems. This paper derives the iteration procedure for the IterEqF update step and shows how the intrinsic nonlinearity of the approach naturally results in a `reset' of the filter's covariance into new coordinates. Monte-Carlo simulations of range-based localisation for a mobile robot demonstrate the improvement in performance relative to a standard EqF, especially during the transient convergence.

papers.title: Amortized Low-Rank Adaptation for Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: World models let agents plan by predicting the consequences of their actions, but changes in the environment can make them inaccurate. We study the problem of adapting a world model to an unknown test-time environment, drawn from a known environment family, using only a few episodes of interaction. Existing approaches trade off computational cost against expressivity, i.e., the range of models a method can produce. For example, in-context learning is computationally cheap but limited in expressivity, and gradient-based adaptation is expressive but computationally expensive. We present CLAW (Context-conditioned Low-rank Adaptation of World models), which addresses this tradeoff by using a hypernetwork to generate low-rank (LoRA) adapters at test time. During pretraining, we simulate adaptation to a variety of environments and jointly train the hypernetwork and base world model. At test time, we freeze the base model and use a forward pass of the hypernetwork to generate adapters from a small batch of test-time transitions. We evaluate CLAW in locomotion and manipulation environment families that vary in dynamics, embodiment, and reward. We show that, using only seconds of test-time data, CLAW outperforms gradient-based adaptation and in-context learning during online adaptation. We also show that CLAW avoids overfitting in data-scarce regimes, that its advantage comes from the expressive adapters rather than context conditioning, and that pretraining the hypernetwork jointly with the base model outperforms training it post hoc.

papers.title: Efficient Vision-Language-Action Management and Serving for Robot Factories
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models show high robotic manipulation capabilities via a two-stage design: a Vision-Language Model (VLM) stage followed by an Action Diffusion Transformer (ADiT) stage. Since robots must meet strict Service-Level Objectives (SLOs) for safety, VLA inference is inherently latency-critical. Meeting these SLOs requires high-end GPUs, yet weight, cost, and power constraints preclude integrating such GPUs on-robot. Prior works offload VLA inference to edge servers that serve many robots on VLA models. However, current VLA systems lack support for multi-request, multi-model execution on a multi-GPU server under SLOs, while existing serving systems for multi-stage models are optimized for throughput and stage disaggregation across separate GPUs, which are ill-suited for the millisecond-scale stages of VLA models. We design Robion, the first VLA serving and management system for multi-robot, multi-model requests on multi-GPU edge servers that meets SLOs. Our serving engine disaggregates the VLM and ADiT stages within a GPU via two streams, dynamically restricting the SMs on VLM stream so ADiT always finds SMs to run alongside it, and co-locates multiple models by sharing these streams across them, prioritizing requests by least remaining SLO time. Our management engine enables flexible model placements on multi-GPU servers, and integrates an intelligent traffic controller that maximizes per-model batching under the chosen placement while bounding each GPU's load to meet SLOs. For individual models, Robion serves on average 6.7$\times$ and 1.5$\times$ higher robot load within 98% SLO attainment over vLLM-Omni, the most widely used multi-stage serving system, and Monolithic, which runs VLM and ADiT as a single pipeline, respectively. In a large-scale experiment of serving 8 different models on a 4-GPU server, Robion can serve up to 64 robots within 98% SLO attainment.

executive_summary: Foundation-model work focuses on aligning task and motion planning data with pretrained VLA distributions and on breaking vision–action shortcuts, directly targeting generalizable manipulation and mobile-manipulation policies.

Multiple papers advance diffusion and world-model-based policies (for rods, deformable linear objects, humanoid traversal, and DIA for fine-tuning), emphasizing long-horizon credit assignment and material-aware control.

Navigation and motion planning see new methods for SE(3) trajectory optimization, context-aware MPC for racing, coverage planning, and battery-aware multirotor planning, along with practical tuning studies for ROS2 costmaps and LiDAR-inertial odometry.
Safety, robustness, and SLAM backend reliability are addressed via neural control barrier functions, multi-session LiDAR SLAM, and distributed stochastic optimal control for swarms under uncertainty.

Manipulation-focused contributions span dexterous in-hand and bimanual control, deformable and cloth manipulation, underwater and coarse grippers, and MagLev-based grasping, supported by large synthetic datasets and geometric priors.

Institution-matched work highlights MIT’s communication-aware multi-robot exploration, Stanford’s distribution-aligned TAMP for data generation, UCSD’s soft “pneumatic neuron” controllers, and NYU’s globally consistent multi-session LiDAR SLAM backend.

institution_matches.title: Communication-Constrained Multi-Robot Exploration With Adaptive Communication Windows
institution_matches.overview: MACE formulates when and where to rendezvous for communication as a vehicle orienteering problem, trading off exploration gain versus travel to communication points. By actively scheduling and valuing communication windows, it reduces total multi-robot exploration time by up to 23% compared to opportunistic or fixed-rendezvous strategies in simulation.

institution_matches.title: DATAFARM: Distribution-Aligned Task and Motion Planning for Fine-Tuning Vision-Language-Action Models
institution_matches.overview: DATAFARM modifies TAMP-generated demonstrations so that robot joint configurations, motion style, and timing better match the data distribution used to pretrain VLA models. This alignment lets TAMP-produced trajectories substantially improve fine-tuning performance, approaching human teleoperation success while retaining strong performance on out-of-distribution deformable tasks.

institution_matches.title: Pneumatic neurons for soft robots enable inflate-and-fire networks for rhythmic motion
institution_matches.overview: The work introduces “Pneu-rons,” soft modules that integrate actuation, logic, and energy conversion, implementing an inflate-and-fire analogue of leaky integrate-and-fire neurons. When arranged in excitatory–inhibitory networks, these elements generate self-sustained, material-level oscillations that can drive adaptive, electronics-free rhythmic locomotion in soft robots.

institution_matches.title: Chain-SLAM: Globally Consistent Backend for Multi-Session LiDAR SLAM via Chained Loop Closure
institution_matches.overview: Chain-SLAM proposes a chained loop-closure scheme that propagates constraints across inter-session keyframes through an adjacency graph, enabling consistent alignment of large multi-session LiDAR maps. Initialized via GNSS-based place recognition and optimized in a unified factor graph, it achieves improved trajectory accuracy and robust cross-session integration without heavy parameter tuning.

topic_matches.title: MoPA: Coordinated Mobile Manipulation via Subsystem-Specific Perception Alignment
topic_matches.overview: MoPA separates perception for base and arm into dual masked visual streams, then couples them in a Mixture-of-Transformers decoder to generate coordinated base and arm action chunks. On ManiSkill-HAB and four real-world mobile manipulation tasks, it achieves state-of-the-art success, showing that subsystem-specific perception alignment improves long-horizon whole-body behavior.

topic_matches.title: STAR: Sparse Tactile Representation Learning in Vision-Tactile-Language-Action Models for Dexterous Manipulation
topic_matches.overview: STAR introduces a 200-hour bimanual dexterous dataset with synchronized vision, tactile, and language, and a VTLA training recipe that sparsifies and predicts tactile tokens. Joint visual–tactile pretraining and sparse future tactile prediction yield a VLA policy achieving 61% average success across four real-robot dexterous tasks after modest post-training.

topic_matches.title: ArtManip: Category-Level Articulated In-Hand Manipulation
topic_matches.overview: ArtManip tackles in-hand manipulation of articulated objects at the category level via procedurally generated articulated models and functional grasps plus a two-stage RL policy. With articulation physics randomization, curriculum design, and latent distillation, the policy generalizes across unseen instances and grasps in simulation and transfers zero-shot to 12 real objects.

topic_matches.title: Global Path Planner with Multi-Model Switching
topic_matches.overview: The planner combines a traversability graph, a heading-aware A* for feasible global paths, and a pure-pursuit controller that switches between kinematic models based on terrain and robot state. Validated on a quadruped and a quadrotor in simulation, the multi-model approach improves path efficiency, robustness, and energy use across diverse terrains.

topic_matches.title: Trajectory Bundle Method in SE(3) for Black-Box Fixed-Wing Aircraft Trajectory Optimization
topic_matches.overview: This work extends the Trajectory Bundle Method to SE(3), constructing bundles in the Lie algebra and propagating them through black-box rigid-body dynamics via exp/log maps. It provides error bounds on SE(3) interpolation and demonstrates derivative-free optimization of an acrobatic, collision-free fixed-wing maneuver through a rotated aperture with unknown dynamics.

topic_matches.title: Driving Context-guided Model Predictive Planning and Control for Autonomous Car Racing at the Limit and Beyond
topic_matches.overview: The authors integrate a Model Predictive Planner and Controller under a Cost Blending state machine that switches context weights for overtaking, nominal driving, and countersteering. On a fully autonomous Superformula racecar, the system achieves lap times within 2% of a top human and robustly handles high-oversteer recovery and aggressive overtakes.

topic_matches.title: A Hierarchical Coverage Path Planning Algorithm for Unknown Environments
topic_matches.institution: University of Science and Technology of China
topic_matches.overview: The proposed online coverage planner incrementally decomposes an unknown environment into subareas organized in a decomposition tree, maintaining an adaptive global coverage tour. A local planner covers each subarea while the tree prioritization balances exploration state and distance, yielding shorter paths and lower overlap than three baselines in simulation.

topic_matches.title: AnchorVLN: Geometry-Anchored Vision-Language Grounding Reasoning for Open-Vocabulary Navigation
topic_matches.overview: AnchorVLN enforces a separation where a VLM proposes semantic cues and geometric tools handle metric reasoning, exposed via an MCP server without metric-bearing APIs. On the CMU VLN Challenge 2026 tasks, geometric anchoring significantly improves instruction following and object-referencing accuracy over direct coordinate estimation while keeping the autonomy stack unchanged.

topic_matches.title: Battery-Aware Predictive Trajectory Planning and Control for Multirotors Under Disturbances
topic_matches.institution: .B is with department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering at University
topic_matches.overview: The framework evaluates candidate multirotor trajectories using closed-loop simulations that include vehicle dynamics, motor models, and a reduced-order battery model, under spatially localized disturbances. By incorporating predicted energy use and battery-dependent actuator limits into planning, it reduces electrical energy consumption and tracking error relative to disturbance-aware baselines, especially at low state-of-charge.

topic_matches.title: Tuning ROS 2 for Energy-Efficient Navigation: Empirical Insights from Costmap 2D Configurations
topic_matches.overview: Through controlled experiments in two warehouse-like environments, the authors study how Nav2 Costmap 2D parameters affect energy usage, CPU load, memory, and navigation performance. They identify configuration regimes that are energy-efficient yet performant, underscoring that environment-specific costmap tuning materially impacts operational endurance of mobile robots.
